newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian exporters rushing to get coffee to port.
newsitem.headline: Colombian exporters rushing to get coffee to port.

text.p: Colombian coffee exporters have begun rushing to get shipments to port ahead of a strike by the country's main truck drivers' union set for April 20, industry sources said.
They said about 420,000 70-kilo bags were being shipped out ahead of schedule in a bid to ensure that April export deadlines would not be missed.

"We've been dispatching April coffee to port since Monday," said one exporter who asked not to be identified by name. "The idea is to have everything in port by April 18 so the strike won't affect us," he added.
Another exporter said the advance shipments could hurt the market, however, because markets would be flooded with Colombian beans over the next week.
"It's going to lower the price because everyone's making advance shipments," he said.

Javier Suarez, head of Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC, said in a statement to the union's rank and file late Tuesday that the April 20 strike was all but inevitable because his latest round of talks with the government had failed to produce any agreement on key demands.
ACC represents about 80 percent of Colombia's truckers.

It set the April 20 strike deadline in March, citing the alleged failure of the government and private transportation companies to fulfill terms of an agreement that ended a crippling 11-day strike last October.
That strike paralyzed virtually all off the country's highway freight, including about 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee.
Industry sources say the April 20 work stoppage will only hurt the coffee sector if it last more than 10 days, after which it would begin to affect May export schedules.
